subject: Re: Urgent: FastChat streaming endpoint latency & errors during peak
messages:
From: Alice Kim <alice.kim@fastchat.app>

Cc: support@fastchat.app
Date: 2028-08-22T08:12:00Z
Subject: Streaming endpoint spike — production impact 17:00-19:00 PDT

Irene / Redwood team,

We saw a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency on your hosted streaming chat endpoint during our evening peak (roughly 17:00–19:00 PDT).

Symptoms: 
- p95 increased from ~220ms to ~550ms; p99 spiked to 1.9s (baseline ~600ms).
- Error rate on SSE connections rose to ~4% (server disconnects/timeouts).
- Throughput dropped for 90s bursts — some messages queued or failed.

Impact: VIP customers are seeing degraded chat responsiveness and we had to degrade the client to fallback polling for a subset of sessions. This is causing immediate CX issues.

I've attached a small trace with request IDs and timestamps: fastchat_stream_trace_0822.zip

Request IDs of interest: fct-7b22a, fct-7b23f, fct-7b240 (samples inside the zip).

Can you confirm you're seeing the same and whether this is a regression on the hosted runtime? We need a short term mitigation and a timeline for a fix.

Thanks,
Alice Kim
Head of Integrations — FastChat
alice.kim@fastchat.app

Irene Choi

From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, eng-oncall@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-22T09:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Streaming endpoint spike — initial triage notes

Team — preliminary findings from the host pool serving FastChat traffic (cluster: us-west-2-fastchat-3):

Observations:
- Host host-12 and host-14 show full-heap GC flurries coincident with p99 spikes (GC pause ~200–400ms). See runtime_gc_0822.log attached.
- Batch sizes for the streaming runtime climbed ~30% above baseline due to a transient increase in short-lived concurrent streams; this pushed latency for a small tail subset.
- KV cache miss rate increased for the past 45m, possibly causing extra recomputation work.
- Error counts: connection resets (RST) correlate with a kernel-level epoll saturation pattern on two nodes.

Immediate mitigations executed (09:00–09:20):
- Flushed prefix KV cache for the FastChat routing pool to avoid recompute storms.
- Disabled large request batching for FastChat traffic (set target batch_size=1 for the pool).
- Increased worker replica count + spun up 4 spare workers into that pool; autoscaler thresholds adjusted temporarily.
- Drained host-12 from the pool for deeper inspection.

Preliminary impact: p99 for the pool improved from ~1.92s -> ~1.22s within 10 minutes after actions; p95 improved to ~360ms. Error rate down to ~1.1%. Still above baseline but trending down.

Next steps:
- If improvement holds, plan to roll a targeted kernel selection rollback (previous stable selection) and monitor for 1h.
- If not, fallback plan: route traffic to dedicated capacity (dedicated pool standby) and schedule a hard rollback to prior runtime build.

I'll continue to monitor and post updates here.

— Jordan
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Date: 2028-08-22T12:20:00Z
Subject: Re: FastChat streaming — mitigation update

Alice / team — quick status update from ops:

What we did (11:40–12:10):
- Performed an immediate targeted rollback of the kernel selection heuristic for the FastChat pool (rolled back to v2028-07-18-kernel).
- Applied a small runtime patch to reduce connection backlog handling latency (mitigation_patch.diff attached).
- Kept batching disabled for the pool and kept increased worker replicas.

Impact observed: 
- p99 dropped from ~1.22s to ~670ms within 20 minutes after the rollback and patch.
- Error rate dropped from ~1.1% to ~0.8%.
- Throughput returned to normal; no new connection resets observed after draining host-12 and applying the patch.

Request: can you validate on your side for the last 30m (sample request fct-7b240) and confirm whether your clients see restored behavior? We'll keep the mitigations until 18:00 PDT and then either gradually remove them or move to a stable fix depending on telemetry.

We'll produce a full postmortem with root cause and action items tomorrow and share a timeline for any SLA credit.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
